**1. Rules for Gemini — `AGENTS.md`**

Current Android Studio Gemini has two mechanisms: per-IDE "Rules" (stored in `.idea/`, not checked into VCS) and `AGENTS.md` files (stored next to your code, IDE-neutral, auto-scanned from project root down). Since you want this project-scoped and inspectable/committable, I used `AGENTS.md` at the project root — drop the file I made into your repo root and Gemini will pick it up automatically on every prompt. It covers both things you asked for: a running numbered NOTES.md (Finished / Next / Judgment calls) that Gemini updates after every change without being asked, and a hard stop before touching any AGP/Kotlin/SDK/library version — it has to explain the change and wait for your OK.

**2. Pulling this Claude session's transcript**

Claude.ai has no per-conversation export button — just a full-account dump. Two ways to get *this* conversation specifically:

- **Just this chat (fastest):** open this conversation → `Ctrl/Cmd+A` to select all → copy → paste into a plain text/markdown file. Or `Ctrl/Cmd+P` → "Save as PDF" for a formatted copy.
- **Official export (whole account):** Settings → Privacy → **Export data** → confirm. You'll get an email with a download link (expires in 24h) containing a JSON of *all* your conversations — you'd then pull out just this one by title/date.

Either way, skim it before sending — TASK.md specifically asks you to strip anything personal.

**3 & 4. Phased Gemini prompts, with logs + a self-maintained transcript**

`GEMINI_PROMPTS.md` has 5 copy-paste-ready prompts (data layer → menu → detail → confirmation → fonts/polish), each pulled from the actual design file's colors, spacing, and copy so Gemini isn't guessing. Each one:
- adds `Log.d(tag = "BentoLand", ...)` at the key checkpoints for that phase, so you can sanity-check via Logcat without waiting on UI,
- ends with a transcript instruction — Prompt 1 has Gemini **create** `TRANSCRIPT.md` and log itself; Prompts 2–5 have it **append** a new dated entry — since Gemini can't export its own session the way Claude Code can.

One thing worth deciding before you start: TASK.md's grading note says get Menu and Detail feeling right over rushing all three screens — so if you're tight on time, Prompt 5 (fonts/polish) is the one to drop, not Prompt 4.

1. ...
2. ...

input.file_text:
# Gemini prompts — Bento Land

Paste these into Gemini in Android Studio one at a time, in order. Each one
assumes the previous one landed. `AGENTS.md` (project root) already covers
NOTES.md upkeep and the "ask before touching versions" rule, so you don't
need to repeat those — this file only adds the transcript-logging step,
since Gemini has no session export of its own.

Before Prompt 1: get the template project building and running (per
TASK.md — take Android Studio's new-project defaults, don't bump anything
to "latest"). That setup doesn't need a prompt.

---

## Prompt 1 — Data layer & networking

```
Set up the data layer for this app.

API: GET https://bentoland-menu.s3.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/menu.json
Plain GET, no auth, returns an array of 10 items. Each item has: name,
name_ja, description, long_description, price (integer yen), calories,
category, tag, sold_out, contents[] (array of strings), image_url, kanji,
and a gradient pair (two hex colors) used as a placeholder tile behind the
photo while it loads and if it never loads.

Please:
1. Add the networking dependency (Retrofit + kotlinx.serialization, or
   whatever this template's stack favors — don't add new dependencies for
   this beyond what's needed to hit a plain JSON GET endpoint).
2. Create a data class matching the JSON shape above.
3. Create a repository that fetches and parses the menu.
4. Create a ViewModel exposing UI state (loading / success with items /
   error) as StateFlow, plus a method to filter by category.
5. Add Log.d calls tagged "BentoLand" for: request started, request
   succeeded with item count, request failed with the error, and each
   category filter change. I'll use these in Logcat to sanity-check the
   fetch without needing the UI built yet.

Don't build any screens yet, just the data layer, and don't change any
Gradle/version numbers to do this — ask first if you think you need to.

Also create a file called TRANSCRIPT.md at the project root. Add a
top-level heading with today's date, then log this prompt and a short
summary of what you did in response, in this format:

## Prompt 1
**Asked:** <one-line summary of what I asked for>
**Did:** <one-line summary of what you built/decided>

Write that first entry now.
```

---

## Prompt 2 — Menu screen

```
Now build the Menu screen using the ViewModel from before.

Design reference (colors/spacing from the design file, in Compose terms):
- Screen background #F7F1E4, page background behind it #EFE7D8.
- Header: 44dp red (#B5342B) rounded-square logo mark, shop name "Bento
  Land" in bold, subtitle "Made fresh this morning · N today" using the
  live item count.
- Category chips row: "All", "Meat", "Fish", "Veggie" as pill-shaped
  filter chips. Selected chip: red background (#B5342B), white text.
  Unselected: white background, 1dp border #E4DAC6, text #6B5F4B. Tapping
  a chip filters the list (client-side, filter by the item's `category`
  field).
- List: white rounded cards, one per item, in a scrolling column. Each
  card: a 62dp rounded tile on the left using the item's `gradient` pair
  as a background gradient with the `kanji` character centered on it in
  white — this is the placeholder, so load `image_url` into the same
  spot and keep the gradient+kanji as what shows while it's loading or if
  it fails. Then item name (bold) with an optional small pill next to it
  for `tag` if present, a small "Sold out" pill if `sold_out` is true,
  a one-line truncated description below, and the price in red
  (formatted like "¥880" / "¥1,280" — thousands separator, yen sign, no
  decimals) on the right with a small chevron.
- Sold-out items: render at ~45% opacity and shouldn't be tappable through
  to an order action (they can still open Detail to view, just can't be
  bought — I'll wire that up in Detail).

Add Log.d (tag "BentoLand") for: screen composed with item count, chip
tapped with which category, list item tapped with item name.

Append a new entry to TRANSCRIPT.md in the same format as before,
summarizing this prompt and what you built. If you had to guess at
anything not covered above (spacing, corner radii, what happens on a
sold-out tap, etc.), note it as a judgment call in NOTES.md per the
project rules.
```

---

## Prompt 3 — Detail screen

```
Build the Detail screen, opened by tapping a menu item.

Design reference:
- Photo header, ~296dp tall, using the item's `gradient` as background
  and the `image_url` photo on top once loaded (gradient stays visible if
  the image never loads — same placeholder behavior as the list tile).
  Overlay the `kanji` character, huge (think ~240sp) and very
  low-opacity white, bleeding off the bottom-right corner as a watermark.
  A circular back button, top-left, semi-transparent white background.
  If `tag` is present, show it as a small pill bottom-left over the photo
  (e.g. "Best seller").
- Below the photo, a sheet with rounded top corners (#F7F1E4) overlapping
  the photo slightly, containing:
  - Item name (large, bold) and price (bold, red) on the same line.
  - name_ja and calories on one line, e.g. "唐揚げ弁当 · 720 kcal".
  - long_description as a paragraph.
  - "IN THE BOX" label, then a white card listing each string in
    `contents[]` as a row (divider between rows).
  - A quantity stepper: "Quantity" label, then a pill with − / count / +.
    Decide sensible min/max yourself (note the choice in NOTES.md as a
    judgment call) and clamp accordingly.
- A sticky bottom bar: red pill button, "Buy now" on the left, the total
  (price × quantity, formatted like "¥1,760") on the right. If the item
  is sold out, this bar should be disabled/replaced with a clear
  "Sold out" state instead of letting the user buy it.

Add Log.d (tag "BentoLand") for: detail screen opened with item name,
quantity changed with new value, buy now tapped with item name/qty/total.

Append a new TRANSCRIPT.md entry the same way. Log any judgment calls
(stepper min/max, sold-out button treatment, etc.) in NOTES.md.
```

---

## Prompt 4 — Confirmation screen & navigation

```
Wire up navigation Menu → Detail → Confirmation → back to Menu, and build
the Confirmation screen shown after "Buy now".

Design reference:
- Centered checkmark-style badge, "Order confirmed!" heading, a small
  Japanese subline below it.
- A white receipt card: order id-style header, a divider, the ordered
  item (icon tile + name + qty + subtotal), another divider, then a
  Subtotal / Tax (8%) / Total breakdown, right-aligned amounts.
  - subtotal = price × quantity
  - tax = round(subtotal * 0.08) to the nearest yen
  - total = subtotal + tax
  - Format all three like the price formatting used elsewhere (¥ with
    thousands separator).
- A muted pickup/fulfillment info row below the card (simple static text
  is fine, e.g. "Pickup — ready shortly").
- "Back to menu" outlined button at the bottom that pops back to the Menu
  screen (clear the back stack so the user can't navigate forward into a
  stale Detail/Confirmation).

Add Log.d (tag "BentoLand") for: confirmation screen shown with computed
subtotal/tax/total, back-to-menu tapped.

Append a new TRANSCRIPT.md entry. Note the tax rounding approach and
anything else you had to decide in NOTES.md.
```

---

## Prompt 5 — Fonts & polish (only if there's time left)

```
Polish pass, time permitting:

1. Apply the two typefaces from the design: Zen Maru Gothic (headings,
   prices, buttons — the bold/black weight text) and Zen Kaku Gothic New
   (body text). Use downloadable fonts via the Android fonts-in-XML APIs
   if that's quick with this template's setup; otherwise bundle the TTFs
   from Google Fonts, or fall back to the system font if either is more
   than a couple of minutes of work. Note which route you took in
   NOTES.md.
2. Double check every price on all three screens is formatted the same
   way ("¥880", "¥1,280" — no decimals, thousands separator).
3. Do a final pass on NOTES.md: make sure "Finished" reflects everything
   actually working right now, and "Next" honestly lists what's missing
   or rough (don't let it drift out of date).

Add a final TRANSCRIPT.md entry summarizing this pass.
```

**1. Rules for Gemini — `AGENTS.md`**

Current Android Studio Gemini has two mechanisms: per-IDE "Rules" (stored in `.idea/`, not checked into VCS) and `AGENTS.md` files (stored next to your code, IDE-neutral, auto-scanned from project root down). Since you want this project-scoped and inspectable/committable, I used `AGENTS.md` at the project root — drop the file I made into your repo root and Gemini will pick it up automatically on every prompt. It covers both things you asked for: a running numbered NOTES.md (Finished / Next / Judgment calls) that Gemini updates after every change without being asked, and a hard stop before touching any AGP/Kotlin/SDK/library version — it has to explain the change and wait for your OK.

**2. Pulling this Claude session's transcript**

Claude.ai has no per-conversation export button — just a full-account dump. Two ways to get *this* conversation specifically:

- **Just this chat (fastest):** open this conversation → `Ctrl/Cmd+A` to select all → copy → paste into a plain text/markdown file. Or `Ctrl/Cmd+P` → "Save as PDF" for a formatted copy.
- **Official export (whole account):** Settings → Privacy → **Export data** → confirm. You'll get an email with a download link (expires in 24h) containing a JSON of *all* your conversations — you'd then pull out just this one by title/date.

Either way, skim it before sending — TASK.md specifically asks you to strip anything personal.

**3 & 4. Phased Gemini prompts, with logs + a self-maintained transcript**

`GEMINI_PROMPTS.md` has 5 copy-paste-ready prompts (data layer → menu → detail → confirmation → fonts/polish), each pulled from the actual design file's colors, spacing, and copy so Gemini isn't guessing. Each one:
- adds `Log.d(tag = "BentoLand", ...)` at the key checkpoints for that phase, so you can sanity-check via Logcat without waiting on UI,
- ends with a transcript instruction — Prompt 1 has Gemini **create** `TRANSCRIPT.md` and log itself; Prompts 2–5 have it **append** a new dated entry — since Gemini can't export its own session the way Claude Code can.

One thing worth deciding before you start: TASK.md's grading note says get Menu and Detail feeling right over rushing all three screens — so if you're tight on time, Prompt 5 (fonts/polish) is the one to drop, not Prompt 4.
